title: Mesh Renderer & Mesh Filter
description: Understand how 3D objects get their shape (Mesh Filter) and appearance (Mesh Renderer).

slides.title: The Duo That Draws 🔺
slides.content:
# Mesh Filter & Mesh Renderer

Every visible 3D primitive (Cube, Sphere, etc.) has these two components:

- **Mesh Filter**: Holds the **mesh data** – the geometry, vertices, triangles that define the shape.
- **Mesh Renderer**: Takes the mesh and **draws** it using a **Material**. It handles lighting, shadows, and culling.

Think of the Mesh Filter as the **wireframe sculpture** and the Mesh Renderer as the **paint and lighting** applied to it.

quizData.question: What does the Mesh Filter store?
quizData.explanation: Mesh Filter holds the reference to the mesh asset that defines the shape.

slides.title: Mesh Renderer Properties 🎨
slides.content:
# Controlling Visibility

Select a Cube and look at its Mesh Renderer:
- **Materials** list – you can assign multiple materials for sub‑meshes.
- **Lighting** – cast shadows, receive shadows, etc.
- **Probes** – reflection and light probes for global illumination.
- **Additional Settings** – motion vectors, dynamic occlusion.

You can toggle the entire Renderer off by unchecking the component (the object becomes invisible).

quizData.question: Disabling the Mesh Renderer makes the object completely invisible but it still exists in the scene.
quizData.explanation: Disabling the Renderer hides the object visually, but it remains active for physics and scripts.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Multiple Materials per Mesh

A single mesh can have multiple materials assigned in the Mesh Renderer's Materials list. Each material corresponds to a sub‑mesh index. This allows different parts of the same model to have different looks.
